scale_guidance: Rate the SUPPORTER only (the side offering emotional support), never the help-seeker.
Use the whole 1-10 range. Reserve 9-10 for exemplary behaviour a trained counsellor would be proud of. Competent but ordinary chatbot replies usually deserve 4-7.
Score every skill independently, using only evidence that appears in the conversation.
Do not reward length, politeness or generic validation. Reward specific, well-timed behaviour that fits what the help-seeker actually said.
If the supporter never shows a skill at all, score it 1-2.

Empathic Understanding.description: How well the supporter conveys a deep understanding of the help-seeker's inner emotional world, reflecting feelings and aligning with their subjective experience.

anchors.1-2: Ignores or misreads the help-seeker's feelings; jumps to advice or gives dismissive, generic statements.
anchors.3-4: Occasional generic sympathy (e.g. 'I'm sorry you're going through this') with little reflection of what the help-seeker actually said or felt.
anchors.5-6: Sometimes reflects feelings fairly accurately, but replies are formulaic, repetitive or only surface level.
anchors.7-8: Consistently reflects feelings accurately and specifically, using the help-seeker's own situation and words; they would likely feel understood.
anchors.9-10: Captures stated and unspoken emotion precisely, adapts to shifts in mood, and conveys understanding without over-claiming or repeating itself.

Encouragement of Emotional Expression.description: Whether the supporter invites, explores and validates emotional experiences, helping the help-seeker articulate and tolerate difficult feelings.

anchors.1-2: Avoids or shuts down emotions: changes topic, minimises, reassures prematurely or says 'look on the bright side'.
anchors.3-4: Rarely asks about feelings; validation is generic or immediately followed by reassurance or advice.
anchors.5-6: Sometimes invites feelings (e.g. 'How did that feel?') but moves on quickly or validates without exploring.
anchors.7-8: Regularly invites and follows up on feelings, validates them, and lets the help-seeker stay with difficult emotions.
anchors.9-10: Skilfully draws out deeper feelings at the help-seeker's own pace, helps name and tolerate hard emotions, and does not rush to fix.

Exploration of Thoughts and Narratives.description: How well the supporter facilitates discussion of the help-seeker's thoughts, beliefs and personal stories through open-ended questions and thoughtful restatements.

anchors.1-2: Few or no questions; lectures or advises; only closed or leading questions; does not engage with the help-seeker's story.
anchors.3-4: Occasional questions, mostly closed or generic, with little follow-up on details the help-seeker gave.
anchors.5-6: Some relevant open-ended questions and restatements, but follow-up is uneven or the story stays superficial.
anchors.7-8: Mostly open-ended, relevant questions and accurate restatements that build on what was said and deepen the story.
anchors.9-10: Questions and restatements consistently uncover beliefs, meanings and background; the narrative becomes noticeably richer, without feeling like an interrogation.

Establish a Trusting Foundation.description: Creates rapport and safety through empathic listening before offering deeper insights or interpretations.

anchors.1-2: Cold, judgmental, scripted or pushy; offers interpretations or advice with no rapport.
anchors.3-4: Polite but impersonal; moves to interpretation or advice quickly; the help-seeker may feel processed.
anchors.5-6: Warm tone and some listening, but rapport is inconsistent or deeper interpretations arrive before safety is built.
anchors.7-8: Warm, respectful and attentive throughout; interpretation or advice comes only after the help-seeker has been heard.
anchors.9-10: The help-seeker visibly opens up and feels safe; the supporter handles hesitation or mistrust gracefully and always listens before interpreting.

Assess Readiness for Insight.description: Notices cues (e.g. confusion, ambivalence) that signal whether to probe deeper, and avoids pushing insight if the help-seeker seems unready.

anchors.1-2: Ignores clear cues; pushes interpretations on an unready help-seeker, or misses obvious openings for deeper exploration.
anchors.3-4: Rarely responds to cues; the timing of deeper probes seems arbitrary.
anchors.5-6: Notices some cues but acts on them inconsistently; sometimes pushes slightly too early or holds back too long.
anchors.7-8: Usually responds to cues, e.g. checks in when the help-seeker is confused or ambivalent, and goes deeper only when they seem ready.
anchors.9-10: Reads subtle cues accurately, explicitly checks readiness (e.g. 'Would it be okay if we looked at...?') and adjusts pace to the help-seeker.

Use Gentle Challenges and Interpretation.description: Offers new perspectives tentatively, encouraging exploration of contradictions or underlying motives rather than dictating answers.

anchors.1-2: Never offers a new perspective, or dictates conclusions, confronts bluntly or tells the help-seeker what they 'really' feel.
anchors.3-4: Rare or heavy-handed reframes; presents interpretations as facts; or only repeats what the help-seeker said.
anchors.5-6: Some tentative perspectives, but they are generic, weakly grounded in what was said, or not followed up.
anchors.7-8: Offers tentative, well-grounded perspectives or points out contradictions in a way that invites the help-seeker's reaction.
anchors.9-10: Insightful, well-timed and tentatively worded interpretations that open new understanding while leaving the help-seeker in control.

Clarify the Desired Change.description: Invites exploration of the exact behaviour, situation or decision the help-seeker wants to address, ensuring a specific goal before action planning.

anchors.1-2: Never asks what the help-seeker wants to change; assumes the goal or advises on an unclear problem.
anchors.3-4: Vague mentions of 'what you want' with no attempt to make the goal specific.
anchors.5-6: Asks about the desired change but accepts vague answers or moves to solutions before the goal is specific.
anchors.7-8: Helps the help-seeker state a reasonably specific goal (which behaviour, situation or decision) before moving to plans.
anchors.9-10: Collaboratively narrows to a clear, concrete goal the help-seeker owns, and confirms it before any planning.

Ensure Readiness and Collaboration.description: Checks the help-seeker's motivation to change and co-creates action plans, respecting self-determination and context.

anchors.1-2: Imposes plans or instruction lists without asking; ignores the help-seeker's context, motivation or objections.
anchors.3-4: Offers plans with only a token 'does this help?'; little attention to motivation or constraints.
anchors.5-6: Sometimes asks about motivation or preferences and adapts a little, but mostly leads the plan itself.
anchors.7-8: Checks motivation and constraints, invites the help-seeker's own ideas and builds the plan together.
anchors.9-10: Fully collaborative: assesses readiness and confidence, respects the help-seeker's choices and context, and adjusts the plan to their feedback.

Brainstorm and Evaluate Options.description: Helps generate multiple ideas, weigh feasibility, benefits and challenges, and align options with the help-seeker's values and needs.

anchors.1-2: No options, or a single directive piece of advice.
anchors.3-4: Lists generic options without discussing fit, feasibility or trade-offs; the ideas come almost entirely from the supporter.
anchors.5-6: Offers several options and mentions pros and cons, but generically and with little input from the help-seeker.
anchors.7-8: Generates multiple options (some from the help-seeker), weighs feasibility and benefits or challenges, and relates them to the help-seeker's situation.
anchors.9-10: Helps the help-seeker generate and compare options against their own values and constraints, and reach a realistic choice or next step they own.
